findings.body:
**Target:** R3/R5; src/sennel.js, src/flow.js, src/help.js
**Issue:** The public sennel entrypoint intercepts valid flow help before flow.js and renders through help.js, whose leaf renderer returns raw entry.help. flow.js's dispatcher shortcut also returns raw entry.help. Verified `sennel flow run abort --help` omits the required structured options.
**Required change:** Specify the public routing boundary explicitly and require src/sennel.js, src/flow.js, and src/help.js to delegate routed flow leaf/group help to the same structured renderer.
**Why blocking:** Without this, one public route can continue returning raw help while another uses structured rows, so the required leaf output and three-route parity cannot be implemented or tested reliably.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec requires three public flow-help routes and identifies R3/R5 plus the flow entry modules, while the finding identifies the missing shared-renderer boundary; the requirement text is the appropriate repair surface.

findings.title: Public flow help bypasses the specified shared renderer
findings.whyBlocking: Without this, one public route can continue returning raw help while another uses structured rows, so the required leaf output and three-route parity cannot be implemented or tested reliably.

findings.body:
**Target:** R2 validation paragraph/R6; src/lib/dispatcher.js, src/lib/command.js, src/flow/lib/base-command.js
**Issue:** parseEntryInput only performs syntax parsing; target/context resolution occurs before command loading, while domain validation is implemented inside individual command execute methods. There is no registry or CommandDefinition validator hook mapping each input to its owner.
**Required change:** Define the per-leaf owner-validation hook and its ordering relative to context/target resolution, or narrow the requirement to validation before command-owned execution/mutation while preserving existing handler validators.
**Why blocking:** Implementing the literal requirement requires moving or duplicating validators, which can change target, logging, lifecycle, and rejection behavior; leaving it unresolved makes the required validation contract unimplementable.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec contains the pre-command validation wording in R2 and the retained execution/validation contract in R6; the finding requires clarifying their owner ordering without authorizing a new validator.

findings.body:
**Target:** R1/T1/R3/R6; src/lib/dispatcher.js and src/lib/cli.js
**Issue:** splitArgsBySpec accepts only canonical option spellings and handles equals syntax only for required options. Although cli.parseArgs has an aliases parameter, parseEntryInput never supplies it, and optional options do not accept equals syntax.
**Required change:** Specify the parser projection rule that normalizes aliases and optional-value forms in parseEntryInput/splitArgsBySpec, passes canonical keys to cli.parseArgs, and defines duplicate/equals behavior.
**Why blocking:** The structured model can display aliases or optional-value rows while the real dispatcher rejects those inputs, so parser/help parity and the required contract tests have no determinate implementation basis.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec names R1, T1, R3, and R6 as the shared option/parser and help owners, and explicitly requires aliases, optional-value forms, and equals syntax to remain parser/help-parity contracts.

findings.body:
**Target:** R6 valid-invocation paragraph and acceptance criteria
**Issue:** R6 defines a valid invocation by syntax, owner validation, and target guards, then requires exit code 0. Existing parser-valid invocations can still fail by documented domain state: get runtime-log returns RUNTIME_LOG_NOT_FOUND with exit 1, and report show returns nonzero when its pointer/report is absent.
**Required change:** Limit exit 0 to successful owner-admitted executions and explicitly preserve expected domain/no-result failures as exit 1, including the representative cases above.
**Why blocking:** A literal implementation would either change existing command semantics or make tests impossible without inventing state that the commands do not require.
findings.evidence: The immutable R6 wording currently describes valid invocations and exit behavior, and the Spec acceptance-criteria collection records the retained exit-1 boundary; the finding requires narrowing the success claim while preserving documented domain failures.

findings.body:
**Target:** R6/T6 runtime-path contract; src/sennel.js, src/lib/container.js, src/lib/dispatcher.js
**Issue:** src/sennel.js's pre-scan recognizes only the separate-token form `--agent-work-dir <path>`. The dispatcher later accepts the equals form, but container.paths.agentWorkDir and logDir have already been frozen by initContainer, and consumers use those paths rather than the parsed input.
**Required change:** State that src/sennel.js must normalize both spellings before initContainer, and identify equals-form support as a required implementation change rather than existing behavior being preserved.
**Why blocking:** Parser tests can pass while the actual runtime path and log precedence differ between the two required forms, making the runtime acceptance contract unsafe to implement.
findings.evidence: The immutable Spec assigns runtime-path ownership to R6 and T6 and explicitly requires both slash and equals agent-work-dir forms to reach the same resolver before container paths are frozen.
